info.description:
Campus API for managing educational resources.

## Error Responses

All error responses follow a consistent envelope format. See the `ErrorEnvelope` schema for details.

## Error Codes

Common error codes:
- `INVALID_REQUEST` (400): Malformed or invalid request
- `UNAUTHORIZED` (401): Missing or invalid authentication
- `FORBIDDEN` (403): Insufficient permissions
- `NOT_FOUND` (404): Resource not found
- `VALIDATION_FAILED` (422): Request validation failed with field-level errors
- `CONFLICT` (409): Resource state conflict
- `INTERNAL_ERROR` (500): Unexpected server error
- `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` (503): Required dependency is down; retry later


## Trailing slashes

Paths are listed exactly as routed (Flask): a path shown with a trailing slash must be requested with it — the no-slash variant answers with a 308 redirect.
info.title: Campus API

get.description:
The plan delta and history the campus-admin Migrations view
renders (#1172): the compute_status diff, per-file approval
metadata (sha256, declared rollback support, docstring
summary) for every pending revision, the full ledger history
(who/when/duration/hash/error per the #746 execution audit),
and whether an apply is in flight.

GET /admin/migrations/
Authorization: a principal holding the 'migrations:read'
scope for this service (#1168: grant rows are instance-scoped
by resource_id naming the service DB).

Returns: {
    "service": <db>,
    "status": [{revision, filename, state}, ...],
    "plan": [{revision, filename, hash, rollback, summary}, ...],
    "history": [{revision, filename, status, applied_at,
                 applied_by, duration_ms, error, file_hash}, ...],
    "running": bool
}

Responses:
    200 OK: dict — the body above.
    403 Forbidden: dict — the caller fails the migrations
        gate for this service.
get.summary: Migration plan and ledger status for this service

post.description:
Sets the apply's cooperative cancel event (#1166): the hook
is checked between migrations, so the in-flight migration
finishes atomically and the remaining revisions stay pending
(the next apply resumes them). 409 when nothing is running.

POST /admin/migrations/abort
Authorization: a principal holding 'migrations:write' for
this service (#1168).

Returns: {"aborting": true}

Responses:
    200 OK: dict — the cancel event is set.
    403 Forbidden: dict — the caller fails the migrations
        gate for this service.
    409 Conflict: dict — no apply is running for this
        service.

Starts the runner's apply for this service's scope in a
background thread and returns immediately: one POST per
staged window, progress lands in the service log and the
ledger, and GET /admin/migrations/ polls `running`/`history`.
The runner's advisory lock (#1166) guards other workers; an
in-process second apply (or a rollback) gets 409. Cancel
between migrations via POST /admin/migrations/abort.

POST /admin/migrations/apply
Authorization: a principal holding 'migrations:write' for
this service (#1168).

Body: {
    "up_to": "008"  (optional — apply only revisions at or
                    below this one; staged windows)
}

Returns: {"started": true, "service": <db>}

Responses:
    202 Accepted: dict — the apply thread started.
    400 Bad Request: dict — unknown `up_to` revision.
    403 Forbidden: dict — the caller fails the migrations
        gate for this service.
    409 Conflict: dict — an apply is already running in this
        worker.

Delegates to the runner's rollback (#1170): migrations
declaring ROLLBACK_SUPPORTED='ddl' run their downgrade();
'backup' migrations restore the envelope named by
`from_backup` (a local path or a bucket://<name>/<key> URI —
the apply's fail-closed backup upload is where the URI comes
from). Undeclared revisions, hash-guarded files and held
advisory locks are refused by the runner; on any failure the
ledger row stays applied. Refused with 409 while an apply is
in flight.

POST /admin/migrations/rollback
Authorization: a principal holding 'migrations:admin' for
this service (#1168 — the destructive cap, granted
sparingly).

Body: {
    "revision": "007",
    "from_backup": "bucket://campus-backups/migrations/005/..."
                   (required for backup-restoration
                   migrations)
}

Returns: {"rolled_back": <revision>}

Responses:
    200 OK: dict — the revision is pending again.
    400 Bad Request: dict — unknown revision (or a backup
        rollback invoked without from_backup).
    403 Forbidden: dict — the caller fails the migrations
        gate for this service.
    409 Conflict: dict — the revision is not applied, cannot
        be rolled back, is hash-guarded, a run holds the
        advisory lock, or an apply is in flight in this
        worker; the message carries the runner's error text.

post.description:
Method:
    POST /bookings

Any authenticated user may book; the booking is attributed to the
principal (client tokens denied — #854). The venue must exist.
The booking starts "pending": deciding it is the venue
authority's call (PATCH status).

The time fields are plain strings rather than schema.Time
annotations on purpose: flask_campus's request unpacking
instantiates str-subclass annotations itself and its coercion
loop does not catch ValueError, so a malformed value would 500
instead of reaching this handler's 400.

Body Parameters (application/json):
    venue_id: schema.CampusID (required)
        The ID of the venue to book.
    description: str (required)
        A description of the booking purpose.
    start_time: str (required)
        Start time in HHMM format.
    end_time: str (required)
        End time in HHMM format.
    date: str (required)
        Booking date in YYYY-MM-DD format.

Responses:
    201 Created: dict
        Booking resource

    400 Bad Request: dict
        {"error": error message} — missing fields, a malformed
        HHMM time or date, or end_time not after start_time.

    403 Forbidden: None
        Returned for client principals (attribution, #854).

    404 Not Found: dict
        {"error": "Venue not found"}

    409 Conflict: dict
        {"error": error message} — an identical booking (same
        venue, date, start and end time) already exists.
post.summary: Create a new venue booking (pending until decided).

delete.description:
Method:
    DELETE /bookings/{booking_id}

Authority (campus#1217): the owner may withdraw their own booking
while it is still pending; once decided (or for anyone other than
the owner), deletion is venue authority — mirroring v1, where
users managed their own bookings and the committee managed
everyone's.

Path Parameters:
    booking_id: schema.CampusID (required)
        The unique identifier of the booking.

Responses:
    200 OK: dict
        Empty object on success.

    403 Forbidden: None
        Not the owner (or the booking is decided) and no venue
        authority.

    404 Not Found: dict
        {"error": "Booking not found"}

Method:

Path Parameters:

        {"error": "Booking not found"}
get.summary: Get a single booking by ID.

patch.description:
Method:
    PATCH /bookings/{booking_id}

Authority (campus#1217): a `status` field is a decision on the
booking — venue authority only (venues.admin globally, or the
venue category's venues.<category-slug>.admin circle). A
description-only patch is the owner's right; anyone else needs
the same venue authority. Venue, date, and times are immutable:
changes there are delete-and-recreate.

Path Parameters:
    booking_id: schema.CampusID (required)
        The unique identifier of the booking.

Body Parameters (application/json):
    description: str (optional)
        New description of the booking purpose.
    status: str (optional)
        "approved" or "denied" (venue authority); "pending"
        resets a decision.

Responses:
    200 OK: dict
        Booking resource

    400 Bad Request: dict
        {"error": error message} — empty body, unknown fields,
        or a status outside the vocabulary.

    403 Forbidden: None
        A status change (or non-owner description change)
        without venue authority.

    404 Not Found: dict
        {"error": "Booking not found"}
patch.summary: Update a booking's description and/or approval status.

Every row is validated before any write, so a bad row anywhere
leaves the calendar untouched. Rows carrying a date that already
has a calendar row are updated in place; the rest are created.

        "Free", "School Holiday", "Public Holiday", "Independent
        Learning Day") or null; `date` is `YYYY-MM-DD`.

Responses:
    200 OK: dict
        {"upserted": n, "days": [written rows, ordered by date]}.

    400 Bad Request: dict
        A malformed row, an unknown day code, or a duplicate date
        in the payload.

put.description:
The day editor's save: both cohorts' codes commit together (v1
semantics — one press saves both dropdowns). The write is
idempotent. Changing a day-code changes which TT day runs on that
date; it does not change which version runs — the timetable
pointers own that.

Method:
    PUT /calendar/{date}

Path Parameters:
    date: str
        The calendar date (`YYYY-MM-DD`).

Body Parameters:
    j1_code: str | None (optional)
        JC1's TT day code, from the vocabulary ("Mon A".."Fri B",
        "Free"); null leaves the field unset (a day with no
        lessons).
    j2_code: str | None (optional)
        JC2's TT day code, same rules.
    term_week: str | None (optional)
        Term-week label (e.g. "T1 W2"), display data.

Responses:
    200 OK: dict
        The written row ({id, j1_code, j2_code, term_week}).

    400 Bad Request: dict
        A malformed date or an unknown day code.

    403 Forbidden: dict
        The caller is not a member of the `timetable.admin` circle
        (only user tokens are eligible).
put.summary: Write one date's day-codes, creating the row if absent.

get.description:
The family-resolution probe: answers exactly what the enforcement
gate answers (campus.api.authz) — the `campus` wildcard, the
primary-group baseline, family-directed edges, and venue-category
narrowing of the group field — reduced to the two effective
fields. The plain membership probe answers the raw containment
question (the value at the hit circle); this endpoint answers the
authority question apps gate on ("is this principal a timetable
admin"), so gate and probe cannot drift.

Method:
    GET /api/v1/circles/{circle_id}/access/{member_id}?category=<slug>

Path Parameters:
    circle_id: str (required)
        The grant circle to resolve against (e.g. the timetable
        family's circle).
    member_id: str (required)
        The principal's user ID (their email, naming their user
        circle).

Query Parameters:
    category: str (optional)
        A venue category; when present, the group field resolves
        narrowed (a matching category subcircle edge is the sole
        source of group-scope authority).

Responses:
    200 OK: dict
        {
            "circle_id": str,
            "member_id": str,
            "wildcard": bool,   # campus:admin (admin everywhere)
            "g": int,           # effective group-scope field
            "s": int            # effective self-scope field
        }

    401 Unauthorized: None
        Returned if the request carries no valid authentication.

    409 Conflict: None
        Returned if the circle does not exist (consistent with
        the members probe).

Notes:
    - Reads stay open (no membership required), consistent with
      the other circles reads: this answers what any client could
      compute from the members listings plus the documented
      resolution algorithm.
    - Answers through resources.circle.resolve_family_access and
      authz.is_platform_admin — the same implementations the
      gates call, so the decisions cannot drift.
    - Emits no events.
get.summary: Resolve a principal's effective access on a grant circle.

Add a member to a circle with a specified access level.

          email-shaped ID).

    403 Forbidden: None
        Returned if the caller is not a member of the
        `circles.admin` circle (only user tokens are eligible).

    500 Internal Server Error: None
        Returned if a storage-level error occurs during the operation.

Notes:
    - Emits the event: `campus.circles.members.add`.
    - Requires membership in the `circles.admin` circle: membership
      editing is privilege escalation once circles gate access.
    - Members are stored as a single `members` dict on the circle
      record, written by read-modify-write: member identifiers may
      be email names, whose dots a nested-field update path would
      misparse.

get.description:
Probe a single membership: the member's access value, or 404 when
unreachable. Resolves transitively through member group circles by
default — the same question campus.api's enforcement gate answers.

Probe a single membership in a circle. An unreachable member is an
expected negative answer (404), not an error: clients use this
endpoint for cheap, fail-closed role checks (e.g. "is this user in
the timetable.admin role circle") instead of fetching the full
members dict. A direct-only answer is available explicitly via
?resolve=direct.

Method:
    GET /circles/{circle_id}/members/{member_id}

Path Parameters:
    circle_id: str (required)
        The unique identifier of the circle to probe.
    member_id: str (required)
        The member identifier to look up, as stored: a circle UID
        or the email name of a user circle.

Query Parameters:
    resolve: str (optional)
        Membership resolution mode. Omit (or "transitive") to
        resolve through member group circles — the default, with
        the same semantics as the enforcement gate (#1202/#1207):
        cycle-safe, stale keys fail closed per key. "direct"
        probes the circle's direct members dict only. Any other
        value is a validation error.

Request Body:
    None

Responses:
    200 OK: dict
        The member's access value within the circle. The default
        (transitive) probe adds resolution detail; ?resolve=direct
        returns the member_id and access_value fields only.
        Example (default / ?resolve=transitive, reached via a
        group):
            {
                "member_id": "teacher@campus.test",
                "access_value": 15,
                "direct": false,
                "via": ["students"]
            }
        Example (?resolve=direct):
            {
                "member_id": "teacher@campus.test",
                "access_value": 15
            }

    404 Not Found: None
        Returned if the circle has no such member under the
        requested resolution mode (the probe's expected negative
        answer). Under the default transitive mode the message
        points at ?resolve=direct, the common cause being callers
        that expected the pre-#1207 direct-only default.

    409 Conflict: None
        Returned if the circle does not exist.

    422 Unprocessable Entity: None
        Returned if resolve has a value other than "direct" or
        "transitive".

    500 Internal Server Error: None
        Returned if a storage-level error occurs while probing.

Notes:
    - Reads stay open (no role membership required), consistent
      with GET /circles/{circle_id}/members/: the probe leaks
      nothing the members listing does not.
    - Resolution answers through the shared membership resolver
      (resources.circle.resolve_member, #1202) — the same
      implementation the enforcement gate uses, so gate and probe
      decisions agree by construction. access_value is the maximum
      across resolving paths; "direct" flags a direct edge and
      "via" lists the containment chain of circle names from the
      probed circle to the member (empty when direct).
    - The default flipped from direct-only to transitive
      (#1207), completing the #1202 switchover ahead of its
      Sunset date; the Deprecation/Sunset headers are retired.
      Direct-only callers must pass the explicit ?resolve=direct.
    - Emits no events.
get.summary: Probe circle membership

post.summary: Move a circle to a new parent.

get.description:
Walk the circle's members transitively and enumerate every
contained user circle (by email name) — the audit question
"who is venues:admin", answered without clients hand-walking
members dicts. Group circles are traversed; user circles are
collected; stale member keys (circle deleted after being added)
are skipped fail-closed without blocking the remaining walk.

Method:
    GET /api/v1/circles/{circle_id}/users

Path Parameters:
    circle_id: str (required)
        The circle whose membership graph to enumerate.

Query Parameters:
    None

Request Body:
    None

Responses:
    200 OK: dict
        {"circle_id": str, "users": [email names, sorted]}

    401 Unauthorized: None
        Returned if the request carries no valid authentication.

    409 Conflict: None
        Returned if the circle does not exist (consistent with
        the members listing).

Notes:
    - Reads stay open (no membership required), consistent with
      the members listing: this enumerates exactly what a client
      could compute by walking the members listings, so it leaks
      nothing new.
    - Emits no events.

post.description:
Lessongroup ids are reused by label across allocations (#592):
a label that already has a group row — from any earlier allocation
— keeps its id, and the row moves to the new allocation, so
subjcombi mappings keyed by lessongroup_id survive version
switches. The payload shape is unchanged (label/members/entries).

Method:
    POST /timetable/

Body Parameters:
    metadata: dict
        Metadata for the timetable, e.g. start and end date.

    data: dict
        The actual timetable data, e.g. lesson groups and entries.

Responses:
    200 OK: dict
       {"data": timetable resource with labeled entries}

    400 Bad Request: dict
        {"error": error message} — missing 'lessongroups',
        missing group keys, or a label repeated within the
        payload (one label anchors one group).

    403 Forbidden: None
        Returned if the caller is not a member of the
        `timetable.admin` circle (only user tokens are eligible).

    409 Conflict: dict
        A payload label is already claimed by two or more group
        rows — historical drift; clean up the duplicate-label
        rows and retry.

delete.description:
Cascades the version's entries, group members and lessongroup rows,
then the version itself. This is the cleanup surface for the
label-drift create 409: stale duplicate-label rows are owned by the
superseded versions that minted them, so deleting those versions
clears the drift. A group row that a later create reused is owned
by that later version and survives.

Refuses to delete the version the current or next pointer names —
move/cancel the pointer first. This action is destructive and
cannot be undone.

Method:
    DELETE /timetable/<timetable_id>/

Path Parameters:
    timetable_id: CampusID
        The ID of the timetable version to delete.

Responses:
    200 OK: dict
        Empty JSON object indicating successful deletion.

    403 Forbidden: None
        Returned if the caller is not a member of the
        `timetable.admin` circle (only user tokens are eligible).

    404 Not Found: dict
        {"error": error message} — unknown timetable_id.

    409 Conflict: dict
        {"error": error message} — the version is the current or
        next pointer target.

        string is rejected — clear with null instead.

    end_date: DateTime (optional)
        The new end date of the timetable.

        `filename` patch attempt, or an empty `label` string.

    403 Forbidden: None
        Returned if the caller is not a member of the
        `timetable.admin` circle (only user tokens are eligible).
patch.summary: Update metadata fields for a specific timetable.

get.description:
Method:
    GET /users/

Authorization (#1226): a user principal with group-read on the
users family (staff:viewer baseline) gets the full list; any
other authenticated user gets the members of circles they can
read (plus themselves); client principals are denied.

Query Parameters:
    q: str (optional) — case-insensitive substring over name and
        id (the id IS the email).
    limit: int (optional) — page size, default 50, capped at 200.
    cursor: str (optional) — the previous response's next_cursor.

Responses:
    200 OK: {"users": [directory records], "next_cursor": str | None}
    502: the campus.auth directory forward failed.
get.summary: Search the user directory (read-only facade).

get.description:
Method:
    GET /users/{user_id}

Authorization (#1226): a user principal with group-read on the
users family sees any record; any authenticated user sees their
own record (self read via the baseline); a scoped caller sees a
record only when it sits in their circle-visible set. An
invisible or absent user is indistinguishable (404) — scoped
callers learn nothing about who exists outside their slice.

Responses:
    200 OK: directory record
    404: the record is absent or outside the caller's slice
    502: the campus.auth directory forward failed.
get.summary: Fetch one directory record (read-only facade).

get.description:
List every circle the given user holds — directly or through
member circles — as absolute paths with their access values: the
inverted membership check. The membership probe answers "is this
user in this circle", this endpoint answers "which circles is
this user in" without clients diffing members dicts (the stopgap
the #1196 prod ops run had to hand-roll).

Method:
    GET /users/{user_id}/roles

Path Parameters:
    user_id: str (required)
        The user's ID (their email account, naming their user
        circle). A user with no resolvable memberships returns an
        empty list, not an error.

Query Parameters:
    None

Request Body:
    None

Responses:
    200 OK: dict
        The user's memberships, sorted by absolute path. Paths
        are derived from containment (root excluded; a
        multi-parent circle appears once per parent chain).
        Example:
            {
                "user_id": "teacher@campus.test",
                "memberships": [
                    {
                        "circle_id": "uid-circle-ab12cd34",
                        "path": "timetable",
                        "access_value": 126,
                        "direct": false,
                        "via": ["committees", "committees.timetabling"]
                    }
                ]
            }

    401 Unauthorized: None
        Returned if the request carries no valid authentication.

    500 Internal Server Error: None
        Returned if a storage-level error occurs while resolving.

Notes:
    - Reads stay open (no membership required), consistent with
      the circles reads: the listing leaks nothing the members
      listings do not.
    - Resolution always goes through the shared membership
      resolver (resources.circle.resolve_member) — the same
      semantics as the enforcement gate and the probe.
      access_value is the maximum across resolving paths;
      "direct" flags an edge on the circle itself; "via" lists
      the containment chain of circle names from the circle to
      the member (empty when direct).
    - User circles are excluded from the listing: membership in
      someone's personal circle is not an authority.
    - Emits no events.
get.summary: List a user's circle memberships as absolute paths

Method:

Responses:

        {"data": [venue resources]}

post.description:
Method:
    POST /venues

Body Parameters (application/json):
    metadata: dict | None (optional)
        Freeform venue facts (name, type, capacity, location, ...).
        Stored verbatim; the shape is deliberately unvalidated
        while the venue schema is fluid.
    notes: str | None (optional)
        Freeform markdown notes.

Responses:
    201 Created: dict
        The created venue.

    403 Forbidden: None
        Returned if the caller is not a member of the
        `venues.admin` circle (only user tokens are eligible).

delete.description:
Method:
    DELETE /venues/{venue_id}

Path Parameters:
    venue_id: CampusID (required)
        The unique identifier of the venue.

Responses:
    200 OK: dict
        Empty object on success.

    403 Forbidden: None
        Returned if the caller is not a member of the
        `venues.admin` circle (only user tokens are eligible).

    404 Not Found: dict
        {"error": "Venue not found"}

get.description:
Method:
    GET /venues/{venue_id}

Path Parameters:
    venue_id: CampusID (required)
        The unique identifier of the venue.

Responses:
    200 OK: dict
        The venue.

    404 Not Found: dict
        {"error": "Venue not found"}
get.summary: Get a venue by ID.

patch.description:
`metadata` replaces the whole dict (merging partial metadata is
the caller's job); `{"notes": null}` clears the note.

Method:
    PATCH /venues/{venue_id}

Path Parameters:
    venue_id: CampusID (required)
        The unique identifier of the venue.

Body Parameters (application/json):
    metadata: dict (optional)
        Replacement metadata dict, stored verbatim.
    notes: str | None (optional)
        Replacement markdown notes; null clears.

Responses:
    200 OK: dict
        The updated venue.

    400 Bad Request: dict
        Empty body, unknown fields, or a non-object `metadata`.

    403 Forbidden: None
        Returned if the caller is not a member of the
        `venues.admin` circle (only user tokens are eligible).

    404 Not Found: dict
        {"error": "Venue not found"}
patch.summary: Patch a venue; given fields replace, absent fields stay.
